turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hello, am I speaking with Mr. Patil from the T Nagar area in Chennai?

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Yes, this is Patil. Who is calling please?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Namaste sir, I am Anirudh from the Community Policing wing. I am calling to inform you about a recent spike in fraudulent calls targeting senior citizens in your neighborhood.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Oh, I have been getting many strange calls lately. Is there something I should worry about?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Please do not worry, sir, but be cautious. We noticed some suspicious activity involving transfers of eighty thousand rupees from several accounts in your locality.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Eighty thousand! That is a lot of money. How do they take it?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: They usually trick people into sharing a one time password or a PIN. I want to warn you that the police or any bank official will never ask you for these details over the phone.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: I see. But what if they say it is for a government verification?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Even then, please do not share your Aadhaar number or bank passwords. If anyone asks for such things, just hang up immediately.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Thank you for telling me, Anirudh. I was getting very confused about these calls.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: You are welcome, Mr. Patil. Just remember that we will never ask for money or codes over a call.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: I will keep that in mind. Thank you for the warning.
